question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Water Resources: Water Scarcity & Management

questions.question_text: What % of Earth's surface is water?
Bhakra Nangal dam is built on which river?
Traditional underground rainwater storage tanks in Rajasthan?
State making rooftop rainwater harvesting legally compulsory?
200-year-old drip irrigation system in Meghalaya uses?
Quantitative vs Qualitative water scarcity.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Quantitative: Physical shortage of water volume. Qualitative: Water abundant but polluted by industrial/agricultural waste.

questions.question_text: What are Tankas?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Underground concrete tanks built inside Rajasthani courtyard houses to store rainwater ('Palar Pani').

questions.question_text: Projections of water scarcity in India by 2025.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: By 2025, nearly 2 billion people globally and vast regions of India will face absolute water scarcity due to population growth and over-exploitation.

questions.question_text: Role of rooftop rainwater harvesting.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Directly collects clean rainfall, recharges local aquifers, and ensures drinking water security during dry seasons.

questions.question_text: Multi-purpose river projects: Advantages vs Disadvantages.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Advantages: Hydroelectricity, irrigation, flood control, inland navigation, fish breeding.
Disadvantages: Reservoir siltation, river fragmentation, loss of aquatic life, land submergence, involuntary human displacement.

questions.case_passage:
Gendathur in Mysuru, Karnataka installed rooftop rainwater harvesting in 200 houses collecting 100,000L annually.
Q1. Village location? (1m)
Q2. How much water harvested annually per house? (1m)
Q3. Significance for dry regions? (2m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Mysuru district, Karnataka.
2. 100,000 liters.
3. Proves decentralized rainwater harvesting ensures water self-sufficiency in dry rural areas.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Water Resources: Dams & Hydraulic Structures

questions.question_text: Mahanadi river dam?
Rain-fed storage structures in agricultural fields of Jaisalmer?
Nehru called multi-purpose dams?
Narmada Bachao Andolan movement target?
Purest form of natural water in Rajasthan?
What is Palar Pani?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The local name for harvested pure rainwater stored in underground Tankas in Rajasthan.

questions.question_text: Name two diversion channels in Western Himalayas.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Guls and Kuls.

questions.question_text: Why multi-purpose dams face social opposition.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dams cause massive displacement of local communities without proper rehabilitation, submerge mature forests, and cause interstate water disputes.

questions.question_text: Historical hydraulic structures in ancient India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Sringaverapura near Allahabad (1st Century BC) channeling Ganga floodwaters. 2. Chandragupta Maurya dam networks. 3. Sophisticated irrigation at Bhopal Lake (11th Century). 4. Hauz Khas tank built by Iltutmish (14th Century).

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Bamboo Drip Irrigation
questions.case_passage:
Meghalaya hill farmers tap stream water using bamboo pipes delivering 20-80 drops/min at plant roots.
Q1. State practicing this system? (1m)
Q2. How water is transported? (2m)
Q3. Drip rate per minute? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Meghalaya.
2. Gravity flow through connected bamboo pipes across hundreds of meters.
3. 20 to 80 drops per minute.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Water Resources: Rainwater Harvesting & Regional Systems

questions.question_text: First state making rooftop RWH compulsory?
Hill diversion channels in Himalayas?
Water scarcity caused by chemical pollution is?
Sardar Sarovar dam river?
Subterranean water table salinization cause?
What are Khadins and Johads?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rain-fed agricultural field storage structures in Rajasthan that allow standing water to moisten soil.

questions.question_text: State one major benefit of Bamboo Drip Irrigation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Prevents water loss from evaporation and delivers water precisely to plant roots in steep terrain.

questions.question_text: How rooftop rainwater harvesting recharges groundwater.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rain falling on rooftops is routed through PVC pipes, filtered via sand/bricks, and discharged into borewells or sumps to recharge aquifers.

questions.question_text: Analyze interstate water disputes caused by multi-purpose projects.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Disputes arise over sharing dam water volume, costs, and release timing. Example: Krishna-Godavari dispute where Karnataka & Maharashtra diversions affect downstream Andhra Pradesh.

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Flood Control & Siltation
questions.case_passage:
Heavy siltation in dam reservoirs reduces water storage capacity, triggering floods during heavy rains as seen in Maharashtra/Gujarat floods.
Q1. Cause of reservoir capacity loss? (1m)
Q2. How siltation triggers floods? (2m)
Q3. Ecological harm of dam siltation? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Heavy sedimentation/siltation at reservoir beds.
2. Silt reduces storage volume, forcing dams to release excess water during heavy rains.
3. Prevents nutrient-rich silt from reaching downstream floodplains.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Water Resources: Water Conservation Strategies

questions.question_text: Freshwater % of total global water?
State receiving highest rainfall with rooftop RWH in Shillong?
Interstate dispute on river Krishna is between?
Inundation canals tap water from?
Water harvesting structure in Barmer?
Why is Shillong's rooftop RWH ironic?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Shillong receives heavy rainfall near Cherrapunji (15 km away) yet faces acute water scarcity, relying on rooftop harvesting for 15-25% of household needs.

questions.question_text: Define Water Scarcity.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Shortage of fresh water relative to human, agricultural, and industrial demand.

questions.question_text: Impact of over-extraction of groundwater via tube-wells.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Causes falling water tables, depletes fossil aquifers, dries up local wells, and leads to arsenic/fluoride contamination.

questions.question_text: Measures for sustainable water management in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Universal adoption of rooftop rainwater harvesting. 2. Watershed management & check dams. 3. Micro-irrigation (drip & sprinkler). 4. Industrial effluent recycling. 5. Public awareness on water conservation.

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Narmada Bachao Andolan
questions.case_passage:
NGO led movement against Sardar Sarovar Dam focusing on environmental issues and displacement of tribal villagers.
Q1. River & dam involved? (1m)
Q2. Main focus of NBA? (2m)
Q3. Demand of displaced people? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Narmada river, Sardar Sarovar Dam.
2. Environmental protection, tree submergence, and tribal displacement.
3. Full land rehabilitation and resettlement.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Water Resources: Comprehensive Water Resource Management

questions.question_text: Dam built on Sutlej river?
Underground rainwater tank capacity in Rajasthan?
Primary source of freshwater input?
Soil degradation caused by dam canal over-irrigation?
National Waterway 1 river?
How do dams cause soil salinization?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Canal over-irrigation raises water tables, bringing subterranean salts to topsoil through capillary action.

questions.question_text: What are Guls and Kuls?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Western Himalayan diversion channels guiding stream water to agricultural terraces.

questions.question_text: Compare traditional rainwater harvesting with modern dam projects.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Traditional RWH: Eco-friendly, low-cost, community-managed, zero displacement.
Modern Dams: High capital, massive storage/electricity, but causes siltation, displacement & ecological harm.

questions.question_text: Detailed breakdown of Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting setup.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Catchment: Rooftop collects clean rainwater. 2. Transportation: PVC pipes carry water down. 3. Filtration: Sand and brick filter cleans debris. 4. Storage: Underground tanka stores water for drinking. 5. Recharge: Overflow recharges well/borewell.

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Tamil Nadu Mandate
questions.case_passage:
Tamil Nadu legally mandated rooftop RWH for all houses with non-compliance penalties.
Q1. State with mandate? (1m)
Q2. Legal requirement? (1m)
Q3. Impact on groundwater level? (2m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Tamil Nadu.
2. Rooftop RWH compulsory for all residential buildings.
3. Raised urban groundwater tables and prevented seawater intrusion in coastal aquifers.
